name: Rebecca Purple
lede: Rebecca Purple is a muted violet added to the CSS color standard in 2014 in memory of Rebecca Alison Meyer, the young daughter of web developer Eric Meyer, who died that year.

sections.title: A memorial color
sections.body:
Eric Meyer's daughter Rebecca, known to friends as Bekka, died in 2014 at the age of six from a brain tumor [1]. At the suggestion of fellow developer Shane Becker, the CSS Working Group added a new named color to the CSS Color Module Level 4 specification in her memory, using the hex value #663399, a shade she liked [1]. That makes Rebecca Purple one of the few CSS keyword colors tied to a named individual rather than to a historical pigment or a generic description [1]. Our library lists both the CSS and Wikipedia sources for the entry, and measures it as a strong violet, 4.2 units from its nearest ISCC-NBS block, close to 1.8P 3.3/13.5 in Munsell notation [2].

Its closest listed library neighbor is plain [[purple]], 5.1 units away, and the color sits between [[byzantium]] and [[royal-purple]] on the wheel, all occupying the same muted violet range rather than the brighter [[amethyst]] or [[orchid]] family [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a close match to Rebecca Purple covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That is unsurprising for a color that only entered any naming system in 2014, long after every painting in the archive was made [3]. A more vivid relative of this same hue, filed in our graph as [[vivid-violet|Vivid rebecca purple]], exists as a separate named variant, one way the color has already begun generating its own family [4].
